title: I See You Rudra: Two Pawn Mates
summary: Let the queen appear, then place the knight where it supports two different pawn mates while the enemy pawns shield your king.

nodes.question: Can the new black queen stop both pawn mates?
nodes.explanation: Nb2 covers a4 and c4 while vacating d3. White threatens a4 or c4; the new queen can change which pawn is right, but cannot stop both.

branches.title: Source finish: the a-pawn gives mate
commentary: Begin after Black promotes on f1. The c7 and c6 pawns are retained: they shield Kb7 from the new queen and block their own king.
Nb2 protects both a4 and c4. The quiet knight retreat prepares two different pawn checks instead of chasing the queen.
Qf2 is the source’s illustrated queen move. It gives no check and cannot prevent a4. The certificate also checks every other legal queen move and c5.
a4# checks b5 with a pawn protected by Nb2. The b4 pawn blocks b4, c3 controls b4/d4, and Kb7 controls a6/b6/c6. Black cannot capture the checking pawn or escape.
branches.explanation: a4# checks b5 with a pawn protected by Nb2. The b4 pawn blocks b4, c3 controls b4/d4, and Kb7 controls a6/b6/c6. Black cannot capture the checking pawn or escape.

branches.title: Independent defense: the queen reaches d1
commentary: Test a queen square that changes the correct pawn choice. This defense and reply are independent additions to the source walkthrough.
Nb2 covers a4 and c4, giving White two possible adjacent pawn checks.
Qd1 controls a4 along d1–c2–b3–a4. That matters: a4 would allow the queen to capture the checking pawn.
c4# chooses the other pawn. Nb2 protects c4; White’s a3 pawn controls a4, while the b4 pawn and black c6 pawn complete the cage. The queen cannot stop an adjacent pawn check.

branches.title: Independent defense: push the shielding pawn
commentary: Test the non-queen defense rather than assuming Black must move its new queen.
Nb2 threatens the two protected pawn mates and leaves Black to choose a legal reply.
c5 is legal and moves the c6 pawn forward, but c5 now blocks the black king’s escape while White’s king still covers c6.
a4# gives the protected pawn check. The newly advanced black c5 pawn supplies an additional self-block rather than opening an escape.

exercises.prompt: What is Nb2 doing besides retreating?
exercises.answer: It protects both a4 and c4 so that the king cannot capture either checking pawn.

exercises.prompt: Why does Qd1 change White’s choice?
exercises.answer: Qd1 can capture a4 along its diagonal. White uses c4 mate instead; the queen cannot capture that pawn or block its adjacent check.
